title: How to Store Cut Avocado So It Does Not Turn Brown

content_html:
Cut avocado turns brown through oxidation when the flesh is exposed to air. Reducing oxygen exposure and keeping it refrigerated slows color change, although it does not stop spoilage indefinitely.

Keep the exposed surface as intact as possible

If you only need half, make a clean cut and avoid bruising the portion you plan to store. The pit protects only the area it physically covers; it does not prevent oxidation across the rest of the flesh.

Add acid and limit air exposure

A thin coating of lemon or lime juice lowers pH and can slow browning. Then press wrap directly against the surface or use a small, tightly sealed container to reduce the amount of trapped air.

Refrigerate promptly

Refrigerate the avocado rather than leaving it out for hours. Cold slows both oxidation reactions and microbial growth, although texture will continue to change over time.

A thin brown layer can be trimmed, but assess the whole avocado

Surface browning alone is not a safety signal. If there is also off odor, slimy texture, mold, or widespread deterioration, discard the avocado rather than judging it only by color.
